blindSummary:
This country's courts have delivered important rulings (a 2023 judgment recognising foreign same-sex marriages; earlier document-change wins for trans people), but same-sex conduct between men technically remains criminalised under the common law (a high court declined to strike it down in 2024, and parliament passed hostile marriage bills), and implementation of the pro-LGBT rulings is documented as unsatisfactory (by a regional litigation centre). The capital has a small organised community (with a national LGBT advocacy organisation); police are unhelpful rather than predatory.

For a visitor: enforcement of the old law is essentially nil, but the legal floor is hostile and the politics are deteriorating.
blindOutOfScope: Common-law criminalisation is unenforced but real; implementation gaps are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: An LGBT+ news outlet (May 2024), also published by a regional litigation centre: argues the courts of this country and of a neighbouring state have issued landmark LGBTQI+ rulings — on decriminalisation and recognition of overseas same-sex marriages — but government implementation is unsatisfactory.

A UN development agency's report (Dec 2024) on a regional human-rights body's LGBT+ resolution and a decade of advancing LGBT+ rights under it - a regional framework document; this country's courts have decriminalised same-sex conduct (2024) and recognised same-sex partners' residency rights, though implementation remains contested.

Regional litigation centre's analysis of transgender rights in this country (2017): constitutional analysis - the equality article omits gender identity and sexual orientation, but its 'other status' category should include them per a UN human-rights committee; a provision of a 1963 births, marriages and deaths registration law allows gender-marker changes on medical evidence, handled case-by-case and 'not problematic' per a national legal-aid centre (2015).

Regional LGBT+ news site (May 2018): this country's first LGBT health centre opened in the capital - a drop-in centre launched by the national LGBT rights organisation on IDAHOT, offering mental health and sexual/reproductive health services; the organisation's director said: 'It is a first.'

Regional LGBT+ news site (Dec 2018): LGBTI+ Pride was celebrated in the capital and in a coastal town - the capital's march (held on World AIDS Day, under a unity slogan) was called the 'biggest pride event' to date, led by a motorcycle club with police escort and a mobile HIV testing clinic.

Foreign national newspaper (June 2014): a local copycat of a neighbouring country's radical-economic-freedom movement was launched here with identical branding but an explicitly anti-gay stance, unlike the neighbouring original.
blindLocalsOnly: The earlier document-change court wins are per-case resident litigation; the implementation gaps documented by a regional litigation centre are resident-facing.
blindTangential: Male same-sex conduct technically remains criminalised under the common law (unenforced) — a formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners; the 2024 legislative backlash signals trajectory.
